newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss franc benefits as mark easing corrected.
newsitem.headline: Swiss franc benefits as mark easing corrected.

text.p: 1610 GMT - The Swiss franc ended slightly firmer against the dollar and mark, with dealers saying the mark's firmness was a correction of recent weakness, which likely was overdone.
"The German economy really isn't in that bad a shape as many people have been saying," one dealer said, referring to the many reports about concerns over German unemployment levels.
The dollar ended easier eventhough higher-than-expected NAPM data supported it in late trade. While there is still room for dollar to firm, upside starting to look limited, dealers said.

* Dollar ends at 1.4748/54 francs vs this morning's 1.4787/97 and Friday's closer of 1.4776/4782. * Mark ends at 87.11/13 centimes vs today's 87.39/41 * Swiss Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) rose to 53.8 percent in February from 51.3 percent.
Dealers say market took no note of figure.
